claims.text: A hybrid approach combining machine learning with reduced-order modeling will significantly decrease the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The hybrid approach will maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost.
Machine-learning algorithms can predict free energies and thermodynamic properties using a reduced dataset from prior elemental and binary studies.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys between 1000 K and 2000 K.
Models trained on existing elemental and binary data can serve as the mediator for predictions in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning models will capture relationships among composition, temperature, and thermodynamic properties.
Capturing these relationships will permit rapid predictions without extensive molecular-dynamics simulations.
The hybrid approach will reduce computational time by at least 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The hybrid approach will achieve fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD for high-entropy systems.
Prediction accuracy will depend on the quality and quantity of the training data.
Variation in training-data quality or quantity may introduce variability into the predictions.
